Treat imported codes and titles as classification data, not diagnostic criteria or medical approval.
Seek NCHS/WHO licensing clarification before expanding the use or distribution scope.

fairUseAssessment.preciseUse: Temporarily download the official NCHS FY 2026 code-description archive and deterministically extract the 1,112 F01-F99 codes, short and long titles, billable/category state, source order, and clearly labeled PsychSim code-prefix navigation into a gitignored local authoring/search cache. Do not copy tabular notes, inclusion/exclusion text, criteria, manuals, or the cache into runtime or distributed repository content.
fairUseAssessment.purposeAndCharacter: The use is noncommercial, private U.S. educational authoring for a personal psychiatry question-bank game. It changes the data container and limits the selection to the psychiatric chapter for lookup, validation, and linking; it does not present the catalog to players, enable clinical coding, or substitute it for a diagnosis manual. Access is restricted to the local authoring workspace.
fairUseAssessment.natureOfWork: The copied elements are terse functional identifiers and factual classification titles from an officially distributed health-data standard. The project excludes the more expressive coding guidance, notes, manual structure, and diagnostic discussion.
fairUseAssessment.amountAndSubstantiality: The full F01-F99 code-title set is used because incomplete lookup would defeat the standardization purpose, but it is a limited chapter-level subset of ICD-10-CM and contains only the minimum fields needed for exact authoring search. No protected diagnostic manual or detailed coding content is copied.
fairUseAssessment.marketEffect: The local cache is gitignored, runtime-excluded, noncommercial, and unavailable to players or repository consumers. It cannot replace an ICD-10/ICD-10-CM licensed product, coding tool, manual, or WHO/NCHS service. The operator must return to the official release for authoritative coding use. Any redistribution, public deployment, or commercial use requires a new rights decision or permission.

decisions.notes: CDC states that WHO owns ICD-10 and authorized NCHS to develop ICD-10-CM for U.S. government purposes. WHO's ICD-10 FAQ says noncommercial/research and internal uses may require a license and directs U.S. modification licensing questions to NCHS. The current ICD-11 Creative Commons terms are not imported into this decision. Until NCHS or WHO grants or confirms a broader permission, PsychSim relies only on the recorded narrow U.S. fair-use assessment for a private local cache.

decisions.notes: The user selected DrugCentral as a formal authoring seed rather than cross-check-only. It does not yet permit AI-assisted processing, runtime redistribution, or commercial distribution. A later implementation must establish an isolated attribution/ShareAlike package and validate upstream provenance before widening those permissions. DrugCentral never determines clinical authority, medical approval, rule activation, or point values.

fairUseAssessment.preciseUse: Retain one original sentence stating that reported palpitations during citalopram treatment warrant further evaluation that includes cardiac monitoring. Do not store, extract, quote, or redistribute label text.
fairUseAssessment.purposeAndCharacter: The use is a highly transformed, noncommercial educational game rule applied to one fictional case. It teaches evaluation of a medication-safety signal rather than serving as prescribing information.
fairUseAssessment.natureOfWork: A regulated drug label is primarily factual and functional, although its exact expression and manufacturer-authored portions may be protected.
fairUseAssessment.amountAndSubstantiality: No label language is copied. One narrow clinical proposition is independently expressed; dosing, tables, warnings structure, and the remainder of the label are excluded.
fairUseAssessment.marketEffect: The original sentence and fictional case cannot substitute for the official label, prescribing database, or licensed drug-information product. Players must consult authoritative sources for real care.

decisions.notes: This assessment covers only the existing original proposition and no source-text ingestion. Broader label use needs a new decision.
